chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of: from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs together, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about wudu (ablution): how much should a man pour over his right hand before putting it into the vessel? He said: “Once after the state caused by sleep and urine, twice after feces, and three times after janabah.”

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَدَثِ النَّوْمِ: the state associated with sleep affecting ritual purity

ai.seo_question: How many times should water be poured on the hand before placing it into the vessel for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states the recommended number of times water should be poured over the right hand before placing it into a vessel when preparing for wudu (ablution), varying according to the type of state of impurity. It reflects the etiquette and legal guidance related to taharah and careful preparation for acts of worship.
